0.reason: the batch path never calls the roadmap, so the saving the section measures holds; the docstring's roadmap claim is corrected by the plan's follow-up section on the batch caches

findings.text: The docstring says the memoised authored-section-headings parse is shared by the roadmap's heading walk and by every wait edge, but reckon/roadmap.py:27 binds authored_section_headings by name at import time, so the wrapper installed on the module attribute at dispatch_batch.py:178 never sees the roadmap's calls; that half of the claimed saving does not happen and the docstring states a mechanism the code does not implement.

The gate counts discovery_state calls and authored_section_headings calls but nothing measures plan-document reads, so reverting plan_document_text to a plain read leaves every assertion true; the text-cache third of the landed change has no test that fails if it regresses.

The fragment quotes 2 state reads and 4 heading parses for four plans at the changed revision; an independent counting plugin over the same gate test at the reviewed head records 3 state reads and 4 heading parses, so the quoted state figure does not reconcile with the run it cites.
